record.paper_title: Homogeneous manifolds whose geodesics are orbits. Recent results and some open problems
record.original_question: Develop the theory of two-step homogeneous geodesics in pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous manifolds, including a pseudo-Riemannian geodesic lemma that characterizes when a curve of the form gamma(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY).o is a geodesic.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M=G/H, \langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)$ be a connected pseudo-Riemannian homogeneous manifold, where $G$ is a connected Lie group acting transitively by isometries on $M$ and $H$ is the isotropy subgroup at a base point $o\in M$. Assume the homogeneous space is reductive, so that the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ of $G$ admits an $\mathrm{Ad}(H)$-invariant decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$, with $\mathfrak{h}=\mathrm{Lie}(H)$ and $\mathfrak{m}$ canonically identified with $T_oM$ in such a way that $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ corresponds to a (possibly indefinite) nondegenerate $\mathrm{Ad}(H)$-invariant symmetric bilinear form on $\mathfrak{m}$.

A smooth curve $\gamma:\mathbb{R}\to M$ is called a two-step homogeneous geodesic through $o$ if it is a geodesic of the Levi-Civita connection and there exist $X,Y\in\mathfrak{g}$ such that
$$\gamma(t)=\exp(tX)\exp(tY)\cdot o\quad\text{for all }t\in\mathbb{R}.$$

Develop a systematic theory of two-step homogeneous geodesics in this pseudo-Riemannian setting. In particular, establish a pseudo-Riemannian geodesic lemma giving necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions on $X,Y\in\mathfrak{g}$ (in terms of the bracket structure of $\mathfrak{g}$, the decomposition $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{h}\oplus\mathfrak{m}$, and the invariant bilinear form on $\mathfrak{m}$) for the curve $\gamma(t)=\exp(tX)\exp(tY)\cdot o$ to be a geodesic of $M$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research direction. Two-step homogeneous geodesics have been developed in the Riemannian and Finsler settings (e.g., Nikonorov; works on two-step homogeneous geodesics in homogeneous Finsler manifolds), but a comprehensive pseudo-Riemannian theory with a corresponding geodesic lemma does not appear to have been completed. Recent works on pseudo-Riemannian geodesic orbit spaces and homogeneous geodesics treat only the one-parameter (one-step) case.

status_evidence.title: Two-step Homogeneous Geodesics in Homogeneous Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Two-step homogeneous geodesics γ(t)=exp(tX)exp(tY).o studied in the Riemannian homogeneous setting.
status_evidence.claim: Two-step homogeneous geodesics have been studied in the Riemannian case, motivating but not resolving the pseudo-Riemannian case.

status_evidence.title: Two-step homogeneous geodesics in some homogeneous Finsler manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Two-step homogeneous geodesics in homogeneous Finsler manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Extensions exist in the Finsler category; the pseudo-Riemannian version remains a stated open direction.

status_evidence.title: The existence of homogeneous geodesics in homogeneous pseudo-Riemannian and affine manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of (one-step) homogeneous geodesics in pseudo-Riemannian manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Pseudo-Riemannian theory currently treats one-step homogeneous geodesics.
